strings.name: Mia Hamm
strings.summary: Hamm's pace, teamwork and scoring made her a leading figure in the United States women's football generation that won two World Cups and two Olympic gold medals. She also helped North Carolina win four NCAA titles and twice won FIFA's world player award. After retiring in 2004, she supported women's sport through her foundation, club investment and advocacy, discussing Angel City ownership again in 2026.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 16, 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: World Cup and Olympic victories helped bring United States women's football to a mass audience.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f1.value: Born in Selma, Alabama; moved frequently with her military family.
strings.highlights.h1.title: World and Olympic titles
strings.highlights.h1.text: Won World Cups in 1991 and 1999 and Olympic gold in 1996 and 2004 with the United States.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education and early training
strings.facts.f2.value: Entered the University of North Carolina in 1989 and helped win four college championships.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Widening participation
strings.highlights.h2.text: Her foundation supports transplant patients' families and opportunities for young women in sport.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Discusses football's future
strings.timeline.t1.text: Talked about US audiences, women's football and investing in Angel City.
strings.timeline.t2.title: National Soccer Hall of Fame
strings.timeline.t2.text: Received a major US football honor after retirement.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Olympic gold and retirement
strings.timeline.t3.text: Won gold in Athens and ended her international and professional playing career.
strings.timeline.t4.title: First FIFA player award
strings.timeline.t4.text: Won the world player award and repeated the following year.
strings.timeline.t5.title: World Cup and foundation
strings.timeline.t5.text: Won the home World Cup and established a foundation for transplant support and women's sport.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Atlanta Olympic gold
strings.timeline.t6.text: Helped the United States win the first Olympic women's football tournament.
strings.timeline.t7.title: First Women's World Cup
strings.timeline.t7.text: At nineteen, helped the United States win the inaugural tournament in China.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Joins North Carolina
strings.timeline.t8.text: Trained under Anson Dorrance and became a key college championship player.
strings.timeline.t9.title: International debut
strings.timeline.t9.text: Joined the senior US team at fifteen, beginning seventeen years of international football.
